questions.question: While preparing to remove an old gas appliance, you smell gas near the appliance shutoff. What is the safest first action?
options: Open nearby windows and continue working
Shut off the gas supply if safe to do so and eliminate ignition sources
Use a lighter to locate the leak
Continue work because old appliances often smell like gas
questions.explanation: The first priority is controlling the hazard: stop fuel flow if safe, avoid ignition sources, ventilate, and report/follow procedures.

questions.question: On a mechanical drawing, a gas line is shown running through a wall, but the site condition shows a structural beam in the same location. What should you do?
options: Drill through the beam without asking
Reroute the gas line wherever easiest
Stop and confirm with the supervisor/designer before changing the layout
questions.explanation: Drawings and site conditions must be coordinated. Unauthorized changes can violate code, engineering, or structural requirements.

questions.category: A3 — Use Common Tools and Access Equipment
questions.question: Why should two pipe wrenches be used when loosening threaded gas piping?
options: To prevent stress on connected fittings and equipment
questions.explanation: One wrench backs up the fitting while the other turns the pipe, preventing damage to connected components.

questions.category: A4 — Use Technical Instruments and Testers
questions.question: A manometer reads 7 in. w.c. What is it measuring?
questions.explanation: Inches of water column is a common unit for low-pressure gas measurement.

questions.category: A5 — Use Codes, Regulations, and Standards
questions.question: If manufacturer instructions are more restrictive than the code minimum, which should normally be followed?
questions.explanation: Manufacturer-certified instructions are part of proper installation and must be followed when they are more specific or restrictive.
